title: Supplementation with a Next Generation Synbiotic in Individuals with Overweight or Obesity: A Triple-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial

mappings.3862374: This project is being externally funded by a supplement company: Pendulum. External funding will be used only in the form of supplement supplies (synbiotic/placebo capsules). There is no monetary compensation from Pendulum.
mappings.3862587: This is a triple-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial to assess the effects of a 12-week supplementation with a next generation synbiotic on body composition, metabolic, dietary, and psychological outcomes in adults (18-45 years old) with overweight or obesity (BMI 25.0-44.9 kg/m2).
mappings.3862588:
Primary outcome: change in body weight (kg) from baseline to 12-week follow-up.
Secondary outcomes: changes in body composition (fat mass, lean mass, body fat percentage via DXA), metabolic markers (fasting glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR, lipid panel, HbA1c), dietary intake (via ASA24 24-hour dietary recall), and psychological variables (anxiety via GAD-7, depression via PHQ-9, cravings via Food Cravings Questionnaire).
mappings.3862589:
The gut microbiome has emerged as a potential contributor to the development of overweight and obesity. Disruptions in the gut microbiome (dysbiosis) have been associated with increased inflammation, insulin resistance, and altered energy metabolism. The gut-brain axis, a bidirectional communication system between the gastrointestinal tract and the central nervous system, has also been implicated in eating behavior, cravings, mood, and anxiety.

Synbiotics, which combine probiotics and prebiotics, have shown promise in modulating the gut microbiome and improving metabolic outcomes. Next generation synbiotics containing novel bacterial strains such as Akkermansia muciniphila, Clostridium butyricum, Anaerobutyricum hallii, and Bifidobacterium infantis may offer enhanced benefits compared to traditional probiotics. Pendulum's next generation synbiotic has been shown to improve HbA1c and postprandial glucose in individuals with type 2 diabetes in preliminary studies.

However, the effects of next generation synbiotic supplementation on body composition, metabolic markers, dietary intake, and psychological outcomes in individuals with overweight or obesity have not been well studied. This trial aims to address this gap by evaluating these outcomes in a rigorous triple-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled design.

References are cited in the text and the bibliography is uploaded as a separate document.

mappings.3862663:
Participants will be recruited from the TCU campus and surrounding Fort Worth community through multiple recruitment strategies:

1. Flyers posted on TCU campus bulletin boards and community locations (e.g., local community centers, gyms, churches)
2. Social media advertisements (Instagram)
3. TCU campus email announcements
4. Word-of-mouth referrals
5. Recruitment tables at campus events

Interested individuals will be directed to contact the research team via phone or email. A member of the research team will provide information about the study and schedule a screening visit if the individual expresses interest.
mappings.3862673:
1. Potential participants will first complete a brief online pre-screening survey (via REDCap) to assess basic eligibility criteria including age, BMI range, and major exclusion criteria. Those who appear eligible based on the pre-screening will be invited for an in-person screening visit.
2. The in-person screening visit will be conducted by the PI or a trained research assistant at Bass Building, TCU campus. During this visit, height and weight will be measured to confirm BMI eligibility, and a brief medical history will be reviewed.
3. Both identifiable information (name, contact information) and non-identifiable health information will be collected during screening.
4. The pre-screening survey will take approximately 5-10 minutes and the in-person screening visit will take approximately 20-30 minutes.
mappings.3862674:
1. Data collected from individuals who are not eligible or who decide not to participate will be destroyed. Their pre-screening survey responses will be permanently deleted from REDCap and any paper records will be shredded.
2. Screening data for enrolled participants will be retained separate from the main study data and stored securely.

Only the person conducting the informed consent and perhaps a second person (an IRB-approved trainee) will be present during the informed consent. Anxiety, depression, and craving questionnaires will be directly answered by the participant in printed copies to facilitate their comfort while answering these personal questions.
mappings.3862692: Participants may withdraw from the study at any time without penalty or loss of benefits to which they are otherwise entitled. If a participant withdraws, data collected up to that point will remain available for research purposes with the intention to use intent to treat analysis. Participants will be informed of this during the consent process.
mappings.3862869:
Participants will complete two main in-person study visits (baseline and week 12) and brief check-ins at weeks 4 and 8.

Baseline Visit (Visit 1, approximately 2-3 hours):
1. Review and sign informed consent
2. Collect demographic information, medical history, and medication/supplement use
3. Anthropometric measurements: height, weight, BMI, waist circumference
4. Body composition assessment via DXA scan
5. Fasting blood draw (approximately 20 mL) for metabolic markers (fasting glucose, insulin, HbA1c, lipid panel) and inflammatory markers
6. Provide stool collection kit with instructions
7. Administer psychological questionnaires: GAD-7 (anxiety), PHQ-9 (depression), Food Cravings Questionnaire
8. Complete ASA24 24-hour dietary recall
9. Randomization to synbiotic or placebo group
10. Distribute 4-week supply of synbiotic or placebo capsules with instructions (2 capsules daily with a meal)

Week 4 and Week 8 Check-ins:
1. Assess supplement adherence (capsule count)
2. Monitor for adverse events
3. Distribute next 4-week supply of supplements
4. Complete ASA24 dietary recall

Week 12 Visit (Visit 2, approximately 2-3 hours):
1. Anthropometric measurements
2. DXA scan
3. Fasting blood draw (approximately 20 mL)
4. Collect stool sample
5. Administer psychological questionnaires
6. Complete ASA24 dietary recall
7. Collect unused capsules for adherence assessment
8. Participant debriefing
mappings.3862806:
1. A DXA (Dual-energy X-ray Absorptiometry) scan will be performed to assess body composition including fat mass, lean mass, bone mineral content, and body fat percentage. The whole body will be scanned.
2. Two DXA scans will be performed per participant (one at baseline and one at week 12). The DXA scan involves a very low dose of radiation (approximately 0.001 mSv per scan, which is less than one day of natural background radiation). The data collected includes total body fat mass, lean mass, bone mineral content, body fat percentage, and regional body composition.

mappings.3862824: Randomization will be performed using a computer-generated randomization sequence. Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either the synbiotic supplementation group or the placebo group. Block randomization will be used to ensure balance between groups.
mappings.3862826: This is a triple-blind study. The participants, the research team members who interact with participants and collect data, and the data analysts will all be blinded to group assignment. The synbiotic and placebo capsules are identical in appearance. The randomization code will be maintained by a designated unblinded team member who is not involved in data collection or analysis. Unblinding will occur only after the database is locked and primary analyses are planned, or in the event of a serious adverse event requiring knowledge of group assignment.
mappings.3862828: Participants in the placebo group will receive capsules identical in appearance to the synbiotic capsules but containing an inert filler. The use of a placebo control is necessary to determine whether any observed effects are attributable to the synbiotic supplementation itself versus placebo effect, time, or other confounders. This design is ethically justified because there is no established standard of care involving synbiotic supplementation for overweight/obesity, and participants in both groups will continue their usual medical care.
mappings.3862942:
The next generation synbiotic supplement used in this study is manufactured by Pendulum and contains the following probiotic strains: Akkermansia muciniphila, Clostridium butyricum, Anaerobutyricum hallii (formerly Eubacterium hallii), and Bifidobacterium infantis, combined with a prebiotic fiber. The supplement is provided in capsule form. Participants will be instructed to take 2 capsules daily with a meal for 12 weeks.

The placebo capsules are identical in appearance, size, shape, and color to the synbiotic capsules and contain an inert filler. Both products are manufactured by the same company (Pendulum) under Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) conditions.

The synbiotic supplement is commercially available as a dietary supplement. It does not require an Investigational New Drug (IND) application.
mappings.3862883: At the end of the study (week 12 visit), participants will be debriefed and informed of their group assignment (synbiotic vs. placebo). They will be told about the purpose of the blinding and the overall study goals. Participants will have the opportunity to ask questions about the study and their results.
mappings.3863061: There are no costs to participants associated with this study. All study procedures, including DXA scans, blood draws, stool collection kits, and supplement capsules will be provided at no cost to participants.
mappings.3863065: Participants will be compensated for their time and effort. Participants will receive a $25 gift card upon completion of each study visit (baseline visit and week 12 visit), for a total possible compensation of $50 for completing the full study. Participants who withdraw before completing the study will receive compensation for any completed visits.
mappings.3863068:
Potential risks associated with participation in this study include:

1. Blood draw risks: Discomfort, bruising, minor bleeding, or rare infection at the venipuncture site. These risks will be minimized by having blood draws performed by trained personnel using standard aseptic technique.

2. DXA scan: Very low radiation exposure (approximately 0.001 mSv per scan, less than one day of natural background radiation). This represents negligible risk. Pregnant women are excluded from the study.

3. Gastrointestinal discomfort: Synbiotic supplementation may cause mild gastrointestinal symptoms such as bloating, gas, or changes in bowel habits. These are typically mild and transient. Participants will be monitored for adverse effects at each study contact.

4. Psychological discomfort: Some participants may experience mild discomfort when completing questionnaires about anxiety and depression levels. If you feel that answering the questionnaires caused psychological distress you have the following resources available:
- If you are a TCU student you can access to psychological health through several ways: psychiatric evaluations, 24/7 telephone counseling helpline, peer support communities, personalized interventions for student athletes, etc. (https://counseling.tcu.edu/student-services/#StudentAthletes)
- If you are not a TCU student, you can find free government support through Texas Health and Human Services by accessing the following link and filling out the form (https://resources.hhs.texas.gov/pages/find-services). This form will be used to provide you with the best phone number to contact based on your needs and based on your location. If you prefer to use a phone number you can call 855-937-2372 and they will help you to get in touch with a health professional.
- If you live in Tarrant County you can directly call MHMR of Tarrant County (My Health My Resources) at 800-866-2465.

5. Loss of confidentiality: There is always a potential risk of data breach, however, only personnel that has been certified and approved by the IRB will have access to the participants and their related data. Samples, questionnaires, and other forms pertaining to the participants will be labeled with an ID that do not include any personal health information of the participant. The document containing the link between the names of the participants and their IDs will be saved in a password protected computer. Informed consents will be saved in the office of the PI which is locked at all times the PI is not present and which is located in a card locked department.
mappings.3863069: Participants may or may not directly benefit from their participation in this project. If in the synbiotic group, participants may have the potential to see beneficial changes in body composition, insulin sensitivity, anxiety, depression, and cravings, however, these are potential benefits and cannot be guaranteed as group designation is random and as research in this synbiotic is still underway. The research outcomes may reveal this synbiotic to be a new therapeutic option for others with overweight or obesity to induce weight loss, insulin sensitivity, and/or diminish anxiety, depression, and/or cravings. Society may benefit from this research because the outcomes from this study will further scientific understanding of the microbiome's effect on overweight and obesity treatment. Furthermore, this clinical trial will provide the scientific foundation and the preliminary data to apply for NIH funding to examine this next generation synbiotic's effect on the gut microbiota through whole metagenome sequencing in stools and on the gut-derived metabolome in blood.

mappings.3863075: If participants withdraw from their study the data collected up to that point will remain available for research purposes with the intention to use intent to treat analysis. Blood and stool samples will be stored in Dr. Ryan Porter's lab located within the Rickel building room 259. For the first stage of the project, blood samples will be analyzed at Dr. Ryan Porter's lab room 259. Once the Nutritional Sciences Department laboratory has been finalized, samples will be transferred to the Nutritional Sciences Department and further storage and analyses could take place here (BASS, room 1203). If enough funds become available to perform the second stage of the study, blood and stool samples (which will be identified by fabricated ID) will be sent to Baylor College of Medicine and to Metabolon for posterior 16S rRNA/WGS and mass spectrometry analyses, respectively. For statistical analysis of the first stage, two sample T-tests will be used to compare within (pre- versus post- values on each group) and between-group (placebo versus probiotic) differences in body composition, adherence, metabolic, dietary, and psychological variables. SPSS will be used for statistical analysis. A p value <0.05 will be considered as statistically significant. Dietetic variables collected via the NCI Automated Self-Administered 24-hour Dietary Assessment Tool including protein, carbohydrate, fat, and fiber will be controlled statistically in the case that significant intra-individual or between-group differences are observed.
